findings.location: Expansive study PDF, physical pages 27-28, Scriptural Date and Location table, Gospel (Mt 21:28-32) dossier (source: sections/80-date-location.tex, the gospel rows)
findings.problem: The longtable breaks inside the Gospel dossier. Its summary row and italic narrated-event row end page 27, and its full-width explanatory row ('Traditional attribution: St Matthew the Apostle ... These are dates of the book, not of the saying') opens page 28 under the repeated header, cut off from the Date cell it qualifies. Page 28 then ends at about 55% of its height before the required fresh page for Appendix: Liturgical Resolution, so the whole dossier would fit there. The explanatory row names its passage and the header repeats, so a reader can recover the link and is not misled. This is a break in the two-tier dossier hierarchy, not a loss of content.
findings.required_result: If the study is reopened for any reason, keep each dossier's summary, event and explanatory rows together with ordinary non-breaking row ends or page-break hints in sections/80-date-location.tex, so that the Gospel dossier moves whole to page 28 and the table breaks only between complete dossiers. Do not change shared table dimensions.

A leaf may not hand-edit these cells, so any fix belongs to the chronology projection's formatting (for example quoting or lower-casing the source label), which is outside this run's repair owners.

The rasters' review-cache records carry these same PDF hashes. Pagination evidence: the synthesis aux (sha256 32e4311c...) places the inventory, overview and all four sense markers on physical page 1, the chronology on page 2, themes from 3 to 4 and the commentary start on 5, and the pages match: a complete twelve-row map in liturgical order, with the two second-reading forms and the two Communion antiphons labelled as options, the options note and exactly four sense rows on page 1; the complete Scriptural Date and Location sheet alone on page 2, legible at the shared compact size; two full pages of substantive Themes and Movement; and an interleaved commentary from page 5 that visibly compares the witnesses question by question, with scope, References, timestamp and colophon ending on page 12. The study's 33 pages (within 20-50) and the concise study's 12 (within 10-12) are physical, with printed folios equal to physical pages. Also checked: the shared Latin Modern, 11-point, 0.75-inch, monochrome baseline (no chromatic pixels on any raster; every font embedded Type 1 Latin Modern in all three PDFs); consistent section and subsection hierarchy; the three keyed interpretation headings, each followed by its own four-senses block in the same nextline form (study pp. 16, 21 and 25); the comparison and branch tables breaking only at row boundaries under repeated headers; no clipped, overlapping or overfull text; no heading stranded at a page foot and no sparse spill page; no columns in either study; the homily's full-width title, two-column ragged speech of six movements recoverable by paragraph and spacing breaks with no citation inside the speech, a page break, and a separate full-width note and References; the final compact rights colophon readable and unclipped on the last page of each PDF, with no spill; no warnings, overfull boxes or undefined references in any of the three logs; PDF title and subject present; clean text extraction with no leaked provenance fields. Limits: installation byte identity and the web edition belong to later stages and were not assessed; this was not a formatting migration, so text-preservation evidence did not apply; source support and argument were judged only so far as confirming that the pages carry them. One advisory (a split Gospel dossier in the study's terminal date sheet) and one observation (the phrasing of the generated chronology labels). Verdict: PASS.
